title: Grid Game
summary: Given a 2D array grid of size 2 x n, where each cell grid[r][c] contains a number of points, two robots start at position (0, 0) and aim to reach (1, n-1).
statement: Given a 2D array grid of size 2 x n, where each cell grid[r][c] contains a number of points, two robots start at position (0, 0) and aim to reach (1, n-1). The first robot can move either right ((r, c) to (r, c + 1)) or down ((r, c) to (r + 1, c)), collecting all points from the cells on its path and setting them to zero. After the first robot has moved, the second robot starts from (0, 0) and aims to reach (1, n-1) by moving right or down, collecting points and also setting them to zero. The first robot aims to minimize the points collected by the second robot, while the second robot aims to maximize its points. If both robots play optimally, determine the number of points collected by the second robot.
constraints: grid has two rows and 1 through 50000 columns of positive points.
Each robot moves right then down once; the first robot zeros its path and minimizes the second robot’s optimal score.
Return the second robot’s score under optimal play.
reference_solution:
def grid_game_second_score(grid):
    top=sum(grid[0]);bottom=0;answer=float('inf')
    for column in range(len(grid[0])):
        top-=grid[0][column]
        answer=min(answer,max(top,bottom))
        bottom+=grid[1][column]
    return answer

hints: Choosing where the first robot moves down leaves only two regions for the second: top cells to the right or bottom cells to the left.
Sweep the down column while maintaining those two sums and minimize their maximum.
Remove current top; candidate=max(top_right,bottom_left); then add current bottom.
The second robot can collect one of the two remaining regions, so its optimum is their maximum; checking every first down-column gives the minimax result.
